summary: Regent is a language whose programs look sequential, with tasks and logical regions whose privileges the type system checks. An optimizing compiler translates it into Legion code and uses index launches, mapping elision and related optimizations to cut runtime overhead.
why_read: It shows how a compiler can place a high-level language over a dynamic task runtime, a direct comparison point for compiler-based distributed programming systems.
main_contribution: A region-based language and optimizing compiler that generates Legion code with performance comparable to hand-tuned C++ Legion on the paper's benchmarks.
main_limitation: Simultaneous (SPMD-style) region access is not implemented, so scaling beyond roughly 10 to 100 nodes requires restructuring by the programmer.
evaluation_method: Single and multi-node throughput against hand-tuned Legion, OpenMP and MPI+Kokkos, knockout experiments and lines-of-code counts
states_relationship_to: Treichler et al. 2013, static type system for Legion [33]
